meters.label: Round trips used before data arrives

frames.narration: A user in Sydney opens a site hosted in Virginia. One round trip across the Pacific takes about 200 ms. Count how many the page needs before anything appears.
Round trip 1: a DNS lookup, if the name is not cached. Here it is counted as a full trip; a nearby resolver can be faster.
Round trip 2 is the TCP handshake, and round trip 3 is the TLS handshake. No page data has moved yet.
Round trip 4 is the actual request and first byte of the response. The server took 20 ms to answer, but the user has waited more than 800 ms.
Fix 1: serve from a nearby edge. The user's handshakes now go to a server 10 ms away, and the edge keeps a warm connection to the origin.
Cached content is answered by the edge directly. Only content that must come from the origin crosses the Pacific, and over an already open connection.

messages.label: cached page, first byte at ~50 ms

frames.narration: Fix 2: fewer handshakes. TLS 1.3 cuts one round trip, and QUIC (HTTP/3) combines the transport and TLS setup, or skips it entirely when the user has visited before.
